title: MiGrATe: Mixed-Policy GRPO for Adaptation at Test-Time

mechanism.domainTask: Online test-time GRPO search for word discovery, molecular optimization, and ARC program induction
mechanism.populationDetail: The core algorithm accumulates generated completions in a common database D; Appendix B.1 separately describes an alternative island-based solution organization.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The core top-k greedy examples are queried from the full historical database; no separate bounded elite archive is maintained.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Core algorithm appends new on-policy and neighborhood samples to D. Appendix B.1's optional island alternative maintains isolated island solution sets and periodically migrates top solutions on a ring.
mechanism.generationDetail: The mixed-policy group uses task-prompt on-policy candidates generated from scratch and neighborhood-sampling candidates conditioned on selected high-reward examples; greedy historical candidates are replayed directly into the GRPO group rather than newly generated.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Numeric rewards guide GRPO updates and top-k historical selection. Dockstring invalid molecules and ARC timeouts receive zero reward; no separate evaluator metadata is described.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Core top-k examples are selected from historical database D for replay and NS prompting, not classical evolutionary parents. Appendix B.1 alternative uses island-local exploration/exploitation selection and periodic ring migration.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The core contribution is mixed-policy online GRPO/test-time policy adaptation using on-policy, replayed off-policy, and neighborhood-generated samples; it is not a conventional evolutionary population loop. Appendix B.1 adds an optional island migration alternative.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/MIGRATE Mixed-Policy GRPO for Adaptation at Test-Time.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: No MIGRATE BibTeX entry or citation was found in the current Survey sources. The optional island-based alternative in Appendix B.1 supports a qualified migration/population mention, but should not be presented as the core algorithm's default. Core top-k selection is prompt/reference selection for GRPO rather than unequivocal evolutionary parent selection.
